Survey Identifies Human Oversight as Crucial for Fair Healthcare Artificial Intelligence

A cross-sectional survey of patients in the United Kingdom has revealed that the absence of human supervision is perceived as the single greatest threat to fairness in healthcare artificial intelligence decision-making. According to the investigation, an overwhelming 89.9 percent of participating patients reported that artificial intelligence decisions that cannot be questioned or challenged by either patients or clinicians would negatively impact fairness. The findings highlight a critical expectation among healthcare recipients that automated clinical tools must remain accountable to human scrutiny rather than operating as autonomous arbiters of patient care.

The research addresses an urgent dilemma arising as the deployment of artificial intelligence in healthcare continues to accelerate. While machine learning and automated systems are frequently introduced with promises to reduce administrative costs and improve operational efficiency across health services, substantial concerns have emerged that these tools could inadvertently perpetuate or exacerbate existing health inequalities. Although prior academic work has explored the degree of general trust patients place in healthcare technologies, less scientific attention has been directed toward understanding how patients conceptualise fairness in artificial intelligence decisions and identifying the specific factors that influence those perceptions.

To investigate these perspectives, the researchers recruited a sample of 149 patients from across the United Kingdom using established public and patient involvement and engagement networks. The cross-sectional study was structured around two distinct operational vignettes designed to represent realistic clinical scenarios: a patient-facing symptom checker tool and a clinician-facing decision-support application focused on cancer treatment. This dual-vignette approach enabled investigators to evaluate whether patient attitudes toward computational decision-making shifted depending on whether the technology interacted directly with the public or functioned within professional oncology workflows.

Participants in the survey evaluated the perceived impact of 13 predetermined factors on the overall fairness of artificial intelligence decisions, while also completing open-ended, free-text responses to identify any supplementary concerns not covered by the standard questionnaire. To analyse the resulting quantitative dataset, the researchers calculated descriptive statistics to summarize demographic and survey variables, applied Pearson’s chi-square tests to detect significant differences in patient attitudes, and estimated statistical associations using ordinal logistic regression models. Qualitative data collected from the free-text responses were independently evaluated using thematic analysis.

The quantitative results showed that the apprehension surrounding unchallengeable automated systems was closely followed by concerns regarding professional clinical guidance and underlying data integrity. A total of 89.3 percent of respondents indicated that artificial intelligence tools developed without clinician input would undermine decision fairness, while 86.6 percent reported that incorrect data recorded in electronic health records posed a severe negative threat to fair automated outcomes. Importantly, patient perceptions regarding these undermining factors remained consistent across both the patient-facing symptom checker and the clinician-facing cancer treatment vignette.

Thematic analysis of the qualitative free-text responses captured several critical dimensions of concern that extended beyond the scope of the 13 structured survey items. Respondents expressed notable anxiety regarding the fundamental accessibility of digital healthcare tools and questioned how automated models would navigate the nuanced diagnostic complexity associated with long-term medical conditions. Additionally, participants raised concerns regarding the ongoing technical maintenance required to keep algorithmic systems accurate over time, as well as the potential emotional loss of human empathy when care decisions become mediated by computational software.

The study authors concluded that patients maintain highly nuanced, multi-dimensional perspectives on fairness that span every phase of the artificial intelligence lifecycle, from initial development through clinical deployment and long-term maintenance. In response to these findings, the researchers offered explicit design considerations for future medical technologies, emphasizing the necessity of engineering human-in-the-loop systems. They concluded that health technologies must be designed collaboratively with end users and possess the technical flexibility to adapt continuously to professional clinical input.

Subject of Research: Patient perspectives on fairness in healthcare artificial intelligence decision-making tools

Article Title: What influences patients’ perspectives on the fairness of AI decision-making tools in healthcare? A cross sectional survey in the UK

Article References: Remfry, E., Tomba, G., Barnes, M. R., Chakraborti, T., Mitra, R., Banerji, C. R. S., & Tzovaras, B. G. (2026). What influences patients’ perspectives on the fairness of AI decision-making tools in healthcare? A cross sectional survey in the UK. BMC Medical Informatics and Decision Making. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12911-026-03906-2
